text.en: Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products. These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster.
text.th: Today, we’re sharing advances in how OpenAI models help engineers design, simulate, and build physical products. These capabilities span mechanical and electrical engineering and end-to-end system design, and are already helping our internal teams test ideas and iterate faster.

text.en: Across these projects, engineers need to bring together mechanical designs, electronics, software, and manufacturing requirements using specialized tools. We’re teaching models to support that work, from preparing drawings and setting up simulations to coordinating changes across disciplines. Our goal is to give engineers more time to explore ideas and improve designs.

text.en: Over the past year, improved frontier model capabilities have helped our internal teams test new ideas and iterate faster, and we are seeing early evidence of these capabilities improving professional workflows in industry as well. We’re working with collaborators to understand where these capabilities can make the biggest difference and what needs to improve. If you’re an engineer, engineering firm, or software vendor involved in the design, simulation, manufacturing, or production of complex physical products, we’d love to work with you to shape this effort around the tools you use and the problems you need to solve.

text.en: Designing a device with Astra
text.th: Designing a device with Astra

text.en: We tested Astra’s state-of-the-art performance⁠ in multimodal and computer use workflows by seeing if we can create a device without any direct human edits. To do this, we used GPT‑6 to define the functional requirements and design the enclosure, printed circuit board (PCB), and software integrations needed to create a device users can use to talk to Codex.

text.en: Accelerating OpenAI hardware teams
text.th: Accelerating OpenAI hardware teams

text.en: OpenAI’s hardware and infrastructure teams use Codex and ChatGPT to create and revise computer-aided design (CAD) models, prepare manufacturing drawings, set up simulations, and review designs. This work spans robotics and compute infrastructure. Since February, model usage across our hardware teams, measured in tokens, has grown 23-fold.
text.th: OpenAI’s hardware and infrastructure teams use Codex and ChatGPT to create and revise computer-aided design (CAD) models, prepare manufacturing drawings, set up simulations, and review designs. This work spans robotics and compute infrastructure. Since February, model usage across our hardware teams, measured in tokens, has grown 23-fold.

text.en: Measuring progress on engineering tasks
text.th: Measuring progress on engineering tasks

text.en: We’re also measuring progress in newer models on tasks that combine coding with engineering knowledge. BenchCAD 2.0 tests whether models can reconstruct 3D parts and assemblies and identify connections in circuit boards. A newer internal model achieved an average score of 0.875, compared with 0.594 for GPT‑6 Astra at its highest reasoning setting. While the engineering lifecycle includes many other elements beyond design, we view improvements in capability here as early evidence of the ability of AI models to positively impact iteration speed for professional workflows.

text.en: Safely deploying with industry collaborators
text.th: Safely deploying with industry collaborators

text.en: We’re working with a small group of industry collaborators to test these capabilities on real engineering problems. Their engineers review model outputs for accuracy and practical use, helping us understand which tasks models can support today and what needs to be improved for safe and reliable use.
text.th: We’re working with a small group of industry collaborators to test these capabilities on real engineering problems. Their engineers review model outputs for accuracy and practical use, helping us understand which tasks models can support today and what needs to be improved for safe and reliable use.

text.en: We’re expanding our collaboration with Chip Ganassi Racing (CGR) to explore how OpenAI models can accelerate engineering and prototyping. Working with its R&D team, we’re testing workflows that turn 3D scans of existing parts into editable CAD models and 2D manufacturing drawings. This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

This is particularly useful when the original design files are unavailable.

text.en: CGR engineers review the models and drawings for accuracy and manufacturability. Their feedback helps us identify where models can reduce manual work and where further improvements are needed.

text.en: We’re also announcing a new research collaboration with Mazda. Our research and Forward Deployed Engineering teams are working with Mazda’s aerodynamics and crash-safety engineers to explore how OpenAI models can help develop and evaluate new vehicle designs.
text.th: We’re also announcing a new research collaboration with Mazda. Our research and Forward Deployed Engineering teams are working with Mazda’s aerodynamics and crash-safety engineers to explore how OpenAI models can help develop and evaluate new vehicle designs.

text.en: The work uses simulations of airflow and structural behavior to explore improvements in performance while accounting for styling and cost. We’ll share more progress and results in the coming months.
